pairs: Factum est autem in sabbato secundo,
as he passed through the grain field,
his disciples were separating the ears of grain and eating them,
by rubbing them in their hands.
Then certain Pharisees said to them,
dicebant illis: Quid facitis quod non licet in sabbatis?
“Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbaths?”
Nec hoc legistis quod fecit David,
what David did when he was hungry,
and those who were with him?
How he entered into the house of God,
and took the bread of the Presence,
et dedit his qui cum ipso erant:
and gave it to those who were with him,
quos non licet manducare nisi tantum sacerdotibus?
though it is not lawful for anyone to eat it, except the priests alone?”
Quia dominus est Filius hominis etiam sabbati.
“For the Son of man is Lord, even of the Sabbath.”
Factum est autem in alio sabbato,
And it happened that, on another Sabbath,
Et erat ibi homo, et manus ejus dextra erat arida.
And there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
Observabant autem scribæ et pharisæi si in sabbato curaret,
And the scribes and Pharisees observed whether he would heal on the Sabbath,
so that they might thereby find an accusation against him.
Yet truly, he knew their thoughts,
et ait homini qui habebat manum aridam:
and so he said to the man who had the withered hand,
“Rise up and stand in the middle.”
And rising up, he stood still.
Interrogo vos si licet sabbatis benefacere,
“I ask you if it is lawful on the Sabbaths to do good,
To give health to a life,
And looking around at everyone, he said to the man,
Et extendit: et restituta est manus ejus.
And he extended it. And his hand was restored.
Then they were filled with madness,
and they discussed with one another, what,
in particular, they might do about Jesus.
Factum est autem in illis diebus,
And it happened that, in those days,
he went out to a mountain to pray.
et erat pernoctans in oratione Dei.
And he was in the prayer of God throughout the night.
et elegit duodecim ex ipsis (quos et apostolos nominavit):
And he chose twelve out of them (whom he also named Apostles):
and Simon who is called the Zealot,
stetit in loco campestri, et turba discipulorum ejus,
he stood in a level place with a multitude of his disciples,
et multitudo copiosa plebis ab omni Judæa, et Jerusalem, et maritima,
and a copious multitude of people from all of Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast,
qui venerant ut audirent eum, et sanarentur a languoribus suis.
who had come so that they might listen to him and be healed of their diseases.
Et qui vexabantur a spiritibus immundis, curabantur.
And those who were troubled by unclean spirits were cured.
Et omnis turba quærebat eum tangere:
And the entire crowd was trying to touch him,
because power went out from him
Et ipse elevatis oculis in discipulis suis,
And lifting up his eyes to his disciples,
for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who are hungry now,
Blessed are you who are weeping now,
Beati eritis cum vos oderint homines,
Blessed shall you be when men will have hated you,
and when they will have separated you and reproached you,
and thrown out your name as if evil,
et ejicerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Filium hominis.
because of the Son of man.
Be glad in that day and exult.
ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cælo:
your reward is great in heaven.
secundum hæc enim faciebant prophetis patres eorum.
For these same things their fathers did to the prophets.
Yet truly, woe to you who are wealthy,
Woe to you who are satisfied,
Woe to you who laugh now,
for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when men will have blessed you.
secundum hæc enim faciebant pseudoprophetis patres eorum.
For these same things their fathers did to the false prophets.
But I say to you who are listening:
Do good to those who hate you.
and pray for those who slander you.
Et qui te percutit in maxillam,
And to him who strikes you on the cheek,
Et ab eo qui aufert tibi vestimentum,
And from him who takes away your coat,
do not withhold even your tunic.
But distribute to all who ask of you.
et qui aufert quæ tua sunt, ne repetas.
And do not ask again of him who takes away what is yours.
Et prout vultis ut faciant vobis homines,
And exactly as you would want people to treat you,
Et si diligitis eos qui vos diligunt,
And if you love those who love you,
what credit is due to you?
nam et peccatores diligentes se diligunt.
For even sinners love those who love them.
Et si benefeceritis his qui vobis benefaciunt,
And if you will do good to those who do good to you,
what credit is due to you?
Et si mutuum dederitis his a quibus speratis recipere,
And if you will loan to those from whom you hope to receive,
what credit is due to you?
For even sinners lend to sinners,
in order to receive the same in return.
And then your reward will be great,
quia ipse benignus est super ingratos
and you will be sons of the Most High,
for he himself is kind to the ungrateful and to the wicked.
Estote ergo misericordes sicut et Pater vester misericors est.
Therefore, be merciful, just as your Father is also merciful.
and you will not be judged.
and you will not be condemned.
and it will be given to you:
et coagitatam, et supereffluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum.
pressed down and shaken together and overflowing, they will place upon your lap.
Eadem quippe mensura, qua mensi fueritis,
Certainly, the same measure that you use to measure out,
will be used to measure back to you again.”
Now he told them another comparison:
“How can the blind lead the blind?
Would they not both fall into a pit?
The disciple is not above his teacher.
But each one will be perfected,
if he is like his teacher.
Quid autem vides festucam in oculo fratris tui,
And why do you see the straw that is in your brother’s eye,
trabem autem, quæ in oculo tuo est,
while the log that is in your own eye,
aut quomodo potes dicere fratri tuo:
Or how can you say to your brother,
sine ejiciam festucam de oculo tuo:
allow me to remove the straw from your eye,’
ipse in oculo tuo trabem non videns?
while you yourself do not see the log in your own eye?
ejice primum trabem de oculo tuo:
first remove the log from your own eye,
et tunc perspicies ut educas festucam de oculo fratris tui.
and then will you see clearly, so that you may lead out the straw from your brother’s eye.
Non est enim arbor bona, quæ facit fructus malos:
For there is no good tree which produces bad fruit,
neque arbor mala, faciens fructum bonum.
nor does an evil tree produce good fruit.
Unaquæque enim arbor de fructu suo cognoscitur.
For each and every tree is known by its fruit.
Neque enim de spinis colligunt ficus:
For they do not gather figs from thorns,
nor do they gather the grape from the bramble bush.
Bonus homo de bono thesauro cordis sui profert bonum:
A good man, from the good storehouse of his heart, offers what is good.
et malus homo de malo thesauro profert malum.
And an evil man, from the evil storehouse, offers what is evil.
Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur.
For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.
But why do you call me, ‘Lord,
and not do what I say?
I will reveal to you what he is like.
He is like a man building a house,
who has dug deep and has laid the foundation upon the rock.
the river was rushing against that house,
and it was not able to move it.
For it was founded upon the rock.
But whoever hears and does not do:
he is like a man building his house upon the soil,
similis est homini ædificanti domum suam super terram sine fundamento:
et facta est ruina domus illius magna.
and the ruin of that house was great.”
